title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is chapter V of Grothendieck's 1986 notes on the 'algebra of figures'. The surrounding pages study a set S with a topology tau, a part T, the complement U, and an auxiliary topology tau' obtained by gluing tau|U with a coarser tau'_0 on T. Page 45 characterises tau'-closed sets. Page 47 tries to characterise tau' by conditions (i)-(iv) and finds a gap ('mais c'est faux!!').

This page specialises to the 'ultratopological' case. I take this to mean Alexandrov-type topologies, where arbitrary intersections of opens are open. Such topological sets are the same as preordered sets J, with closed sets read as down-sets or up-sets. A map phi of ultratopological sets then has an associated monotone map phi*: J' -> J between the underlying posets.

Corollary 1: if the topology of J' is the quotient of that of J (phi* surjective, read as an effective quotient), then phi is an 'imm.', probably an immersion. In context this most likely means the induced map on the figure algebras is injective.

Corollary 2: if phi* is surjective with connected fibres, then again phi is 'imm.'.

Corollary 3, the main point. Call phi* 'homotopically proper' if every inverse image phi*^{-1}(J_{<=x}) of a principal down-set is weakly contractible. Then phi* is an 'Iso' (some invariant is carried isomorphically). This is exactly the hypothesis of Quillen's Theorem A for posets.

The proof sketched is the standard localisation step. One reduces to the case where I (a down-set or closed piece of J) has a greatest element x, with x in I, and must show that its preimage I' is weakly contractible. Grothendieck takes the unique element x' of I' lying over x. He shows x' is a greatest element of I', using that x' lies in I' \ U' and a closure comparison between the closures C-bar' and C-bar. A poset with a greatest element is contractible: 'OK!'.

The final restatement: if phi* is homotopically proper with weakly contractible fibres (equivalently, a universal weak homotopy equivalence), then 'Iso pour phi'. This is a poset or Alexandrov-space version of Quillen A, or McCord-type results, phrased as a 'proper base change' criterion. It parallels the aspherical, proper and smooth functors of Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs.
errors: The reduction step is only sketched. Why one may reduce to I having a greatest element (a Mayer-Vietoris or local-to-global argument over principal down-sets) is not written out.

The claim that the element of I' over x is unique is asserted without justification. It would need injectivity over x or the specific gluing structure (x' in I' \ U'), which is not visible on this page.
The meanings of 'imm.' and 'Iso pour phi' (which invariant is preserved) are not stated on the page, so the corollaries are partly ambiguous.
The next page shows the general characterisation of tau' feeding these corollaries is incompletely proved, and partly 'faux'. These corollaries may therefore rest on an unproven property e).

ideas.what: Identifying topologies closed under arbitrary intersections ('ultratopological') with preorders, and transferring topological statements to posets
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov spaces / finite spaces and posets

ideas.what: Fibres phi*^{-1}(J_{<=x}) weakly contractible implies phi* induces an isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Quillen's Theorem A for posets / aspherical (homotopically proper) map
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) and Les Dérivateurs, in the aspherical/proper functor formalism (the general notion, not this exact page)

ideas.what: Reduction to the case of a greatest element: a poset with a maximum is contractible
ideas.modern_name: cone / contractibility of posets with a top element
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (categories with final object are aspherical)

ideas.what: A quotient map of ultratopological sets (phi* surjective, possibly with connected fibres) gives an 'immersion' of figure algebras
ideas.modern_name: injectivity of pullback on constructible functions / figure algebras under surjections

missed.claim: Grothendieck applies a Quillen-A type 'homotopically proper' criterion to maps of Alexandrov (ultratopological) spaces inside the 'algebra of figures' project. This links his homotopy-theoretic asphericity formalism with a combinatorial or constructible algebra of figures. The link is mild and largely anticipated by McCord/Quillen and by later work on finite spaces and constructible functions.
missed.quote: Corollaire Si φ* est homotopiquement propre à fibres faiblement contractiles (dans un sens équivalent d'homotopie faible universelle), Iso pour φ.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a small piece of evidence that the 1986 'Algèbre des figures' was meant to connect with the Pursuing Stacks / Dérivateurs asphericity theory, which matters for historians. Mathematically the statement is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a sketched poset version of Quillen's Theorem A in Grothendieck's 'ultratopological' language, with routine proofs. The only interest is historical: it shows asphericity ideas inside the 1986 figure-algebra notes.
transcription_corrections: 'Isof-Isof' is probably 'Iso f – Iso f' or a struck-through 'Iso' repetition; read as 'Iso pour φ*'.
'J_{≤x}': the manuscript shows a symbol corrected between '<' and '≤'.
'c = (Ultratopologiques)': the 'c =' is probably a stray or abbreviated 'cqfd' closing the previous proof, not an equation.
'l'unique point élément de I' au-dessus de x': the image reads roughly 'l'unique élément de I' au-dessus de x'.
'dans x∈I f.c.' should read 'I admet un plus grand élément x∈I (f.c.)', with 'f.c.' = faiblement contractile inserted.
